headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill aims to shift the financial burden of grid infrastructure and capacity costs for large energy users, like data centers, away from residential ratepayers to the high-load users themselves.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer advocates, environmental groups, some lawmakers seeking ratepayer protection.
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial energy users.
news_headline: Governor Amends Bills Shifting Costs Onto Data Centers
news_summary: Governor Spanberger signed HB 1393, but suggested amendments that removed a direct cost shift for capacity auctions, instead giving the State Corporation Commission more authority to ensure data centers pay their fair share. The bill still aims to save residential customers money and renew a power line burial program.

headline: Data Center Water Consumption Reporting Mandate
short_summary: This legislation requires water users providing water to data centers to report the total volume of water consumed, including reclaimed water, to the State Water Control Board, enhancing transparency for water resource planning.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, water conservation advocates, local communities, Nature Forward.
news_headline: Virginia Adds New Restrictions, Tracks Data Center Water Use
news_summary: Governor Spanberger signed bills, including SB 553, to regulate data centers by tracking their water usage. This measure aims to provide critical data for regional water supply plans, especially given Virginia's high concentration of data centers.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill empowers local governments to impose stricter zoning, siting, and noise regulations on data centers, requiring impact assessments and mitigating negative effects on nearby residential areas.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residential groups, environmental and conservation groups, historic preservation advocates.
opponents: Data center developers, tech industry trade groups, chambers of commerce.
news_headline: Manassas Tightens Data Center Zoning Rules Amid Concerns
news_summary: Localities like Manassas are tightening zoning rules for data centers, addressing concerns about noise, appearance, and proximity to residential areas. HB 153 supports these efforts by requiring impact assessments for large data centers and allowing localities to mandate noise studies and other reviews.
